Document Intelligence Platform — Test Reference Document
=========================================================

Introduction
------------

This document serves as a plain-text reference fixture for the DocForge test suite.
It contains multiple sections, varied sentence lengths, and enough content to exercise
the chunking pipeline end-to-end without relying on external files.

Section 1: Background
---------------------

Document intelligence refers to the automated extraction, classification, and
structuring of information from unstructured documents. Modern pipelines combine
optical character recognition, layout analysis, natural language processing, and
vector embeddings to transform raw files into queryable knowledge bases.

Key challenges include:
- Heterogeneous input formats (PDF, DOCX, HTML, images).
- Variable layout quality: scanned documents, multi-column text, embedded tables.
- Language ambiguity: abbreviations, domain-specific terminology, cross-references.

Section 2: Architecture
-----------------------

The DocForge pipeline is organised into sequential stages (S0 through S6):

S0 — Ingest: normalise the input to a canonical PDF representation.
S1 — Parse: extract the structured Intermediate Representation (IR) using Docling.
S2 — Enrich: route figures, tables, and scanned blocks to OCR/VLM providers.
S4 — Chunk: split the IR into retrieval units respecting section boundaries.
S5 — Contextualise: prepend title and heading breadcrumb to each chunk's embed text.
S6 — Embed & Index: generate BGE-M3 dense+sparse vectors and upsert into Qdrant.

Each stage fingerprints its inputs with blake3; unchanged inputs skip re-execution
via the NodeCache (Merkle-DAG cache). Provider API calls are separately cached
by the ProviderCallCache keyed on (provider_id, input_hash).

Section 3: Retrieval
--------------------

Hybrid search combines:
1. Dense retrieval: cosine similarity over BGE-M3 dense vectors.
2. Sparse retrieval: BM25 keyword matching over BGE-M3 sparse vectors.
3. Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF): fuses the two ranked lists into a single score.

The fusion weights (dense, sparse) are configurable per request, enabling real-time
exploration of the dense–sparse trade-off without re-indexing.

Conclusion
----------

This fixture file is intentionally multi-section and verbose to produce several
meaningful chunks when processed by the S4 chunking stage.
